items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: There's a fella by the name of Zoo Robertson. I didn't talk about him.

ctx.x: Well, when you started, did you, I know Bunk tells about when he started on trumpet. He studied at school and had a Mexican teacher and made him study solfetch. Yes, yes. The sight reading. Yes, sight reading. Did you have to go through that before you took up your instrument? Or how did you think?

Well, it seemed like to me that, I don't know, the man said that it was natural for me. See? Because I have a large lip and I played in a large mouthpiece. And he said it was natural for me that I didn't have the words. And he told me, he said, you're going to come to be one of the best trombone players of tears. I didn't think he'd do it. I just played just to, you know. Yeah, he could tell. Make a little air. He could tell, you know, from the way I handled the instrument. He said, you'll be one of the best of…
You were talking about Zoo Robertson? Zoo Robertson, yeah.
